title: Weighted routing and compatibility probing playbook for customer-driven model onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a playbook and lightweight feature set that lets customer-submitted model variants be evaluated and routed into production via weighted routing + active compatibility probing. The goal is to reduce manual triage for large enterprise requests while preserving safety and stability: automated probe runs, short canary windows, automatic pin recommendations, and explicit eval gates for semantic/regression checks.
background: We receive frequent enterprise requests to add third-party or quantized model variants. Current intake is manual, causing long lead times and operational risk. Recent incidents showed regressions after naive pinning (INC-2025-08) and customer SLA breaches for latency-sensitive routes. PM and ENG aligned on building an intake lane that automates compatibility checks, produces a recommended pin probability, and provides an operator-visible audit trail.
deliverables: Compatibility probe runner (light-weight eval harness that runs smoke suite + latency/profile checks)
Weighted routing UI control in Console (percent-based split with auto-suggestions)
Pin recommendation engine (score and human-readable signals)
Eval gate checklist template (semantic tests, hallucination risk, latency, memory usage)
Playbook doc for PM/SE to approve onboarding (steps, risk buckets, rollback actions)
acceptance_criteria: Probe runner executes on submitted model artifacts and emits pass/fail + metrics (latency, mem, top-level quality checks)
Console shows suggested initial weight and risk tier; operator can launch canary with <24h window
Pin recommendation includes at least three signals (compatibility score, latency delta, eval regression delta)
Automated rollback triggers if error rate or latency exceed configured thresholds during weighted rollout
Playbook covers customer communication templates, required artifacts, and minimum evals per risk tier
out_of_scope: Full automated pinning without human approval; deep safety model fine-tuning; on-prem installer changes (Private deployment will reuse probe artifacts later).
risks_and_mitigation: False negatives in probe -> mitigation: require human review for medium/high risk tiers
Customer expectation mismatch -> mitigation: include explicit SLA/behavior notes in onboarding checklist
Probe adds latency to intake -> mitigation: probe runs asynchronously and results stored; gating only applied for PRD canaries
Hidden infra cost (large probe suites) -> mitigation: cap probe compute and prioritize tests by signal value
implementation_notes: Use existing eval harness in ENG-19822 as baseline; implement a thin adapter that runs smoke tests and a 1k sample semantic regression set
Leverage runtime telemetry hooks to capture latency/kv-cache behavior in canary runs, avoid synthetic benchmarks only
Design Console changes with 'suggested weight' callout and one-click canary start; include link to probe report
Pin recommendations are advisory strings, not enforced mutations to customer configs
Data retention: probe reports stored for 90 days for audit and rollback investigation

open_questions: What is the minimum semantic eval set size that yields stable regression signals for diverse customers?
Should the probe runner run in a sandboxed Private environment for on-prem customers?
How tightly should suggested weights map to our historical A/B canary heuristics (e.g., 5/25/50 percent increments)?
